lens: AN INTRADAY NEWS-REACTION LANE: PREREG-EVL-11 draft, label "intraday", the IDN lane. The events are single-company Benzinga articles that the House first stores during the session. The lane buys by a marketable limit order in the first House minute after its live decision, about a minute after the House stores the story. It sells by a marketable limit order at 15:40 ET. It is long-only, whole shares, learning size, and judged by PREREG-EVL-6's frozen screen. Intraday 8-Ks and a grid of entry delays, horizons and filters are kept as free records for the meta-learners. The replay is the SIP NBBO touch at the rule's own send instants. That is the honest replay for a continuous-session fill, and it is what Done's fill item reads. By construction the lane holds nothing at either auction. So it trades only the cash that sits idle between the auctions (about 45% of equity after the open, per A118). It takes no dollar, slot, reservation or name from any auction row. It adds no metered compute, because the verdicts it reads are ones the day-news rows already ask. Everything is in ~/Work/.ltcm-main/goal-2026-10-19/evl10/intraday/: calib/ holds the synthetic runs with their SHA256SUMS, and count_idn.py is the captain's outcome-free count script. I did not run count_idn.py and did not read the House store.
design:
PREREG-EVL-11 (draft): THE INTRADAY NEWS-REACTION LANE (IDN)

A. THE CLOCK. Code facts are from origin/rel/1019h; the latency figures come from calib/lat_idn.py.
A1 The times.
  - T_pub is Benzinga's created_at for news, or EDGAR's acceptance time for an 8-K.
  - T_rcv is received_at, the House's first store of the item (league/events/news.py `record`; filings.received_at).
  - THE LANE'S KNOWABLE TIME IS T_rcv. It is not created_at + 2 min, which is the auction lanes' rule. No decision can come before the House's own store.
A2 What the code does today.
  - The record pass runs every 2 min (house.py RECORD_EVERY) and is bounded at 90 s. It reads EDGAR's two current feeds first, then the news "since the newest stored less 5 minutes".
  - The lane's turn starts on each publish (house.py publish_seconds = 60). It runs one task a turn, on the one-slot feeds lane (league/house.py `_lanes["feeds"] = Semaphore(1)`).
  - THERE IS NO INTRADAY DECISION. A story stored during the session is first bought at that session's closing auction: PREREG-EVL-2/-4/-5 close rows, decided at close - 14 min, with cls buys until 15:49 ET.
  - lat_idn.py, today: an article is stored p50 99 s / p95 161 s after created_at at an assumed 5 s Alpaca lag (124/186 s at 30 s; 184/246 s at 90 s). Its first possible real order is hours later: about 4.8 h for a story stored at 11:00 ET.
A3 The lane's path (harness H1).
  - A FAST TASK runs on its own House background lane, "intraday" (Semaphore(1)). It starts on every House tick (config.json tick_seconds = 30) from open + 5 min to close - 60 min.
  - Each turn: one news page, the filter, the verdict asked at once, and the intent written (decided_at).
  - The book sends the order in its next minute (live.py: the book is "handed the minute's start, three seconds past the wall minute").
  - lat_idn.py, the order at the venue after created_at: p50 65 s / p95 97 s at a 5 s Alpaca lag; 90/122 s at 30 s; 150/182 s at 90 s.
  - After the House stores the item: p50 42 s / p95 69 s, whatever the lag.
  - The Alpaca REST lag and the pass durations are ASSUMED. count_idn.py measures received_at - created_at, outcome-free. No rule depends on them.
A4 The instants.
  - decided_at is the stored time the fast task wrote the intent.
  - T_e = the first wall-minute start strictly after decided_at, plus 3 s.
  - T_x = close - 20 min + 3 s: 15:40:03 ET, or 12:40:03 on an early close.
  - Sessions, early closes and DST come from the store's `sessions` table.
A5 Market data (league/data_plan.py, Alpaca's free Basic plan).
  - Real time is IEX only: `market.stocks` = GET v2/stocks/snapshots?feed=iex through the gateway, giving latestQuote and latestTrade. IEX bars are dropped.
  - SIP history is served only when 16 min or older. snapshots?feed=sip and quotes/latest?feed=sip answer 403.
  - The plan allows 200 requests a minute, shared with the book.

B. THE EVENTS
B1 AN IDN(D) CANDIDATE is an article A that meets all of (i) to (vii):
  (i) received_at in [open + 5 min, close - 60 min) of session D, i.e. 09:35-15:00 ET.
  (ii) live: received_at - created_at <= 10 min (news.LIVE_WITHIN).
  (iii) exactly one symbol.
  (iv) its issuer is ELIGIBLE for D by the LIVE rule (the `eligibility` table). An issuer not yet judged is judged in the fast task by universe.py's live rule, at most 10 new issuers a turn. In addition: universe adv20 >= $20,000,000; prev_close >= $5.00; and prev_close <= 0.05 x E, where E is the book's equity at the previous close. With that price cap one whole share fits every band, so the shadow is exactly what money can buy.
  (v) FRESH: among rows stored before decided_at, no article naming the ticker (with any number of symbols) was created in [P's close, created_at(A)), and no 8-K of the CIK was accepted in that span. P is the session before D. A must also be the issuer's first candidate of D.
  (vi) NOT A PRICE STORY: the headline does not match KW_MOVE = (shares are trading|stock is (moving|trading|up|down)|why is|shares (rise|fall|jump|drop|slide|soar)|trading (higher|lower)|\bmovers?\b), case-insensitive. This is copied verbatim from PREREG-EVL-7's frozen kw_move (evl7/reader/features_spec.py, sha256 b2f3aaaa).
  (vii) A QUOTE AT DECISION: the IEX snapshot read for the decision shows bid > 0 and ask > 0, uncrossed, with a quote time in D and within 60 s of decided_at; (ask - bid)/mid <= 60 bp; and ceil_cent(1.003 x ask) <= floor_cent(1.25 x the previous SIP close).
  The event id is `idn:<article id>`.
B2 THE LIMIT: L = ceil_cent(1.003 x the IEX ask at decision), stored with its snapshot in idn_quotes.
  - IEX's ask is at or above the NBBO ask, so L is marketable by at least 30 bp at decision.
  - L sits inside the gateway's frozen cap of 1.25 x the previous close.
B3 One event per issuer per D per program. Cooldown: PREREG-EVL-1 section 5 with A72, i.e. an issuer the program holds or held (real or shadow) within the last 5 sessions is skipped.
B4 NO BACKFILL, NO CATCH-UP, NO RE-DECISION.
  - An event exists only if the House decided it live. An outage removes the events it hid: an entry minutes after a story cannot be made after its window.
  - This departs from PREREG-EVL-1 section 3 ("an outage removes nothing"), and the departure is stated. The removal is by the clock, never by a price.
  - The report counts outage minutes: fast-task gaps over 90 s inside the window.
  - Consequence: the seats' records start at the release's first live session. Unlike A117's files, the CODE is the critical path. Freeze and ship together.
B5 THE LANE HOLDS NOTHING AT EITHER AUCTION.
  - Entries start at 09:35, after the open cross has printed.
  - Exits run 15:40-15:45, before the close decision at close - 14 min.
  - So its lots never take an auction row's cash, ROOM slot, A85 reservation or name, and `_event_gate`'s same-auction sale skip never sees them.
  - A lot still held at 15:44 is sold in the closing auction: the fallback, counted and alarmed.
B6 SETTLED CASH: every intraday buy is sized on S, never above the account's current cash, where
  S = cash at the 09:25 pre-open reading - today's buy fills of every lane (at cost) - every working buy's worst cost - cash_reserve_usd ($50).
  - So no intraday buy is paid with today's unsettled sale proceeds. This is the cash account's good-faith rule; US settlement has been T+1 since May 28, 2024 (SEC Rule 15c6-1 as amended).
  - The O1 open buys are placed before the open's sale proceeds exist, so they are unaffected.

C. EXECUTION AND THE REPLAY
C1 ENTRY. In the book's minute that starts at T_e:
  - a LIMIT BUY, time_in_force "day", whole shares, limit L, client id `idn-<program>-<sha8(event)>`;
  - cancelled at the first book minute at or after submitted_at + 60 s when not fully filled (a whole-share partial fill stands);
  - never re-priced and never chased;
  - A80's venue-cancel re-send applies once, at the same limit, before T_e + 60 s;
  - an order not sent by T_e + 60 s is missed and recorded with its reason.
C2 EXIT.
  - At T_x: a LIMIT SELL of the whole lot at floor_cent(0.997 x IEX bid), using an IEX bid of this session no older than 60 s; otherwise a market sell.
  - At 15:42, if still open: cancel, and resend at floor_cent(0.990 x IEX bid), or market.
  - At 15:44, if still open: cancel and send a market-on-close sale (cls).
  - After that, the existing fallback ladder (book.py) takes over, every rung alarmed.
C3 THE REPLAY. These are the shadow's prices, and Done item 7's "replay". They are read at night from SIP history: GET v2/stocks/<sym>/quotes?feed=sip through the gateway, under data_plan's 16-minute clamp. The prevailing quote at T is the last quote with t <= T.
  - entry_px = the NBBO ASK prevailing at T_e.
  - exit_px = the NBBO BID prevailing at T_x. When no quote lies within 60 s of T_x, it is the official closing print as score.py reads it.
  - Both prices are stored on score.py's adjusted basis (raw x score._ratio(symbol, D)). done.py's fill item then divides them back to raw unchanged.
  - TRADABLE iff: entry_px exists with its quote within 60 s of T_e; the NBBO at T_e is two-sided and uncrossed; its spread (ask - bid)/mid <= 100 bp; entry_px <= L (the order was marketable at T_e); and exit_px exists.
  - r = exit_px x (1 - (m_x + f)/1e4) / (entry_px x (1 + m_e/1e4)) - 1. In score.after_cost_return's terms: cost_entry_bp = m_e and cost_exit_bp = m_x + f.
  - spread_entry_bp and spread_exit_bp are recorded.
  - stress_r = r with each side's half-spread charged once more.
  - b = the benchmark's return over the hold: the close of the last SIP 1-min bar ending at or before T_x, divided by the one ending at or before T_e, minus 1. The benchmark is IWM when adv20 < $50M, else SPY (universe.py).
  - a = r - b.
  - m_e and m_x (the slippage margins) = max(5 bp, the largest value ever reached by mean + 1.645 x sd/sqrt(n) of the lane's last 50 real gaps on that side). They are recomputed at each settlement from fills stored before it: forward-only and never falling.
  - f = max(0.30 bp, the running maximum of posted sale fees / proceeds).
  - REAL GAP: entry = fill / ask(T_e) - 1; exit = 1 - fill / bid(T_x). Positive means real money did worse.
C4 MEASURED NIGHTLY (records for the report; no judge reads them):
  - fill rate;
  - send lag (submitted_at - T_e);
  - signed gaps per side;
  - markouts (NBBO mid at T_e + 60 s and + 300 s, against the fill);
  - non-fill selection: the shadow r of TRADABLE events whose real order missed, beside those that filled.
C5 EXEC HOLD, which guards Done's two-sided fill item.
  - Trigger: the lane's last 30 real fills on a side have a signed mean gap above +10 bp or below -10 bp, or its last 30 sends filled under 60%.
  - Effect: new real entries stop for the rest of that session and the next. The shadow goes on.
  - A third hold within 20 sessions stops real entries until a release (alarm).
  - No captain step lifts a hold.

D. THE PROGRAMS (version 1, REGISTERED_AT_11)
D1 EVL-IDN-READ-C (seatable).
  - Events: IDN(D) candidates whose PROMPT-NEWS verdict is ok with score >= 2, answered within 120 s of received_at. The prompt and model are PREREG-EVL-1's frozen ones (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, temperature 0); the first stored answer is final.
  - Decided at the fast task's first turn after the answer.
  - rank_key = -(seconds from D's open to T_e), so the earliest ranks first; ties go to the earlier received_at, then the event id.
  - The shadow keeps the EARLIEST K = 20 events a session.
  - Entry at T_e, exit at T_x. Control: CTRL-IDN-ALL-C.
D2 EVL-IDN-CONF-C (seatable only when section G holds both seats; otherwise registered as a free record of the same text).
  - Events: IDN(D) candidates with any verdict, received_at <= close - 90 min.
  - Decided at the fast task's first turn at or after received_at + 30 min.
  - Taken when 1.010 <= m30/p_pre <= 1.200. m30 is the IEX mid at that decision, under B1 (vii)'s quote rules. p_pre is the close of the last SIP 1-min bar ending at or before received_at - 60 s, which is readable by then.
  - L is set from that decision's IEX ask. Rank and K = 20 as in D1.
  - Entry at that decision's T_e, exit at T_x. Control: CTRL-IDN-ALL30-C.
D3 CONTROLS (free records, never seated).
  - CTRL-IDN-ALL-C: every IDN(D) candidate, decided at the first turn after receipt.
  - CTRL-IDN-ALL30-C: every candidate received by close - 90 min, decided at +30 min, with no price condition.
  - Above 60 events a session, each keeps the 60 with the smallest sha256("IDN-CTRL|<D>|<event>").
D4 FREE RECORDS: never seated, never screened as a seat, no figure on the site. They are settled from SIP 1-min bars, with the event's own NBBO spread at T_e charged half on each side, plus the same fees and margins.
  - REC-IDN-<filter>-<entry>-<exit>, over CTRL-IDN-ALL-C's events.
    - Filters: all; s>=2; s=3; s<=0; upgrade|initiate; pt; raise|beat|guidance; fda|deal|contract|buyback|dividend; downgrade|cut|miss|offering (PREREG-EVL-7's KEYWORDS); benzinga; fiscal.ai; confirm +1.5%; unmoved +-0.5%; drop <= -1.5%; adv20 >= $50M.
    - Entries: T_e, +5, +15, +30, +60 min.
    - Exits: +15 min, +60 min, T_x.
  - REC-IDN-STALE: candidates that fail only the FRESH rule (hash cap 30), entry T_e, exit T_x. This is the intraday reading of Tetlock 2011's stale news.
  - REC-IDK-READ-C and REC-IDK-ALL-C: intraday 8-Ks with items 1.01, 2.01, 7.01 or 8.01 and no 2.02, fresh and eligible under B1. They use the PROMPT-DOC score >= 2 that the 8k-day family already asks. Entry at the first turn after the fetch, exit at T_x.
  - These are the meta-learners' families for a later file: PREREG-EVL-8 part B reads every lane's records.

E. THE JUDGES
E1 PREREG-EVL-6 sections 1-3 ALONE judge every seat, under its "LATER VERSIONS" clause, unchanged:
  - one block per entry session, never overlapping;
  - y_s = min(n_s, 14) x (B_s - 10 bp);
  - looks at blocks 22, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50 and 60;
  - alpha 0.020 / 0.006 / 0.001;
  - the top-14 guard on the rank above, so the earliest 14 = what Probe money buys;
  - p_I <= 0.10;
  - the control condition: screen.CONTROLS gains READ -> CTRL-IDN-ALL-C and CONF -> CTRL-IDN-ALL30-C;
  - RETIRE, runs, Sized, demotion and the money stop as written.
E2 FINALITY: a session is final once its settlement receipt holds every intent of the session (B4: nothing can arrive later). Late SIP data delays a settlement, never its as-of session.
E3 Nothing here edits PREREG-EVL-6, done.py or any judge. The settlement writes `outcomes` rows that screen.py and done.py read as they read every other file's rows.
E4 LANE STOP. It is stricter-only: the goal's pivot, made earlier.
  - When: at the lane's 200th and 400th settled TRADABLE seat events, pooled across seats in settlement order.
  - Test: the 95% session-block bootstrap upper bound of mean r (2,000 resamples; seed sha256("IDN-STOP|<count>")).
  - Trigger: the bound is below -10 bp at 200, or below 0 at 400.
  - Effect: every seat is retired (why "lane stop"). Controls and records go on.
  - The goal's own pivot at 400 Probe+ events stands beside it.

F. REAL MONEY
F1 Bands and ROOM.
  - Learning: 2% of E a position, one share up to 5%, max_open 8 a program a session.
  - Probe: 3.5% with S2's at-size rule (reach_bar 0.8), max_open 14 (PREREG-EVL-6 section 6).
  - Sized: 10%, max_open 8.
  - ROOM inside the lane: Sized, then Probe, then learning; then D1 before D2; then rank.
  - The lane meets no auction.
F2 Every buy passes, in turn:
  - book.size_entry with the walls: 10% a name book-wide on the walls' equity, the 100% book, the loss budget at max(0.10, 1.65 sigma sqrt(h)), and cash = S from B6;
  - real_block: grant, kill switch, daily and drawdown stops, reconciliation, pause;
  - the EXEC HOLD;
  - the paper proof's BUY stage;
  - the gateway (H8).
F3 The lane's order line: equity_money.event.intraday.max_orders_day = 60 (bounds 0-80), counting entries and exits.
  - It sits beside the auction line of 150, inside MAX_DAY_ORDERS 300 and MAX_DAY_OPEN_ORDERS 250.
  - An entry leaves room for its own 3 possible exit orders.
  - An exit is never stopped by the line.
F4 Full-size shadow: D1 and D2's K = 20 events a session, each at its band's target.
F5 PAPER PROOF (A68's pattern). On the release's first live session, at 09:40 ET: one 1-share intraday buy of an eligible name on alpaca-paper through the new route, its 60 s cancel path, and its 15:40 sale. Real entries wait for the BUY stage; sales never wait.
F6 The owner's walls are unchanged. The lane is long-only: no short sales, margin, options, fractional shares or extended hours.

G. FALSE PASSES AND THE BUDGET (PREREG-EVL-6 section 5)
G1 The charge is 0.13 for each seat version at REGISTERED_AT_11, and 0.13 for each later run, charged when it starts and only when the budget holds it. Records and controls are free.
G2 SEAT RULE AT THE FREEZE. LEFT = 3.9 - the SEATING sum that R3's validator reads at the freeze.
  - LEFT >= 0.26: D1 and D2 both seat.
  - 0.13 <= LEFT < 0.26: D1 alone seats; D2 is registered as a free record. A later file may seat D2, counting only later events.
  - LEFT < 0.13: the file is not frozen unless the captain restates the budget, with its cost stated. Each 0.13 is one more expected false pass; a false Probe here costs about $2.8 a session (cost_idn.py).
G3 Arithmetic today, on EVL-8's budget8 basis:
  - EVL-6 1.95 + EVL-7 0.26 + EVL-8 0.65 + EVL-9 0.26 = 3.12.
  - With A104's three births (0.39): 3.51, so LEFT = 0.39 before READER-2 and this file.
  - So the likely case is D1 alone.

H. READINGS RECORDED BEFORE THE FREEZE
H-a The fast task asks PROMPT-NEWS at once for IDN candidates. These are the day-news rows' own verdict rows: the same event, prompt and model, first answer final. No score changes. The only effect is that more DAY(D) articles are answered by PREREG-EVL-5's close decision. That decision skips an issuer whose article has "no PROMPT-NEWS answer by then", so fewer issuers are skipped, which is the frozen text's intent.
H-b The lane uses intraday-idle cash only (B5, B6). No earlier row's sizing reads it.

I. THE HONEST PRIOR (literature, cited only where I am sure)
- Busse & Green (2002, JFE 65(3)), CNBC stock reports: prices respond within seconds; positive reports are incorporated within about a minute, negative ones over longer.
- Patell & Wolfson (1984, JFE 13(2)), wire earnings and dividend news: most of the price adjustment comes within 5-10 minutes.
- Chordia, Green & Kottimukkalur (2018, RFS 31(12)): macro news is priced by low-latency traders within milliseconds.
- So a House that is 1-2.5 min late and pays the spread is late for the first reaction. What can remain is underreaction drift:
  - Tetlock, Saar-Tsechansky & Macskassy (2008, JF 63(3)): firm news predicts returns with slight underreaction.
  - Chan (2003, JFE 70(2)): monthly drift after news, reversal after no-news moves.
  - Heston & Sinha (2017, FAJ 73(3)): news predicts returns over the following days.
- Attention effects push the other way:
  - Barber & Odean (2008, RFS 21(2)): individuals are net buyers of attention-grabbing stocks.
  - Berkman, Koch, Tuttle & Zhang (2012, JFQA 47(4)): attention stocks earn high overnight returns that reverse intraday.
  - Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019, JFE 134(1)): overnight and intraday returns pull against each other.
  - Tetlock (2011, RFS 24(5)): stale news reverses. FRESH and KW_MOVE exclude stale and price stories.
- Gross-Klussmann & Hautsch (2011, J. Empirical Finance 18(2)): spreads widen and liquidity falls around news. That is the cost C3 measures.
- Expected outcome, stated: the most likely result is that the seats pay tuition and retire. The swing is priced in section 'cost'.
why_it_compounds:
1. IT ADDS EVENTS PER DOLLAR AT NO COST TO ANY OTHER ROW. About 45% of equity sits idle between the auctions (A118). A learning seat puts 16% of E to work: 8 lots of $38, at 2-8 real events a session. A Probe seat can put up to 49% to work: 14 lots of $66.
  - B5 means the lane never holds a lot at an auction, so it takes no auction row's cash, slot, reservation or name.
  - B1 (v), the FRESH rule, makes its issuers disjoint from the same day's open-entry news, earnings and 8-K rows.
  - Every event is a new, issuer-independent draw, which is the goal's "more independent events per dollar".

2. IT IS FREE IN METERED DOLLARS. There is no new model call: the PROMPT-NEWS verdicts are the day-news rows' own, asked earlier (H-a), and the 8-K records reuse the 8k-day family's PROMPT-DOC. The IEX and SIP reads sit inside the Basic plan. Under A102 the lane costs no sessions; its price is tuition, $0.6-1.5 a session a seat at zero edge (cost_idn.py).

3. IT GIVES THE HILL-CLIMBER A NEW AXIS: TIME INSIDE THE SESSION. The D4 grid crosses about 15 filters with 5 entry delays and 3 horizons, settled nightly on real NBBO spreads, plus stale-news and intraday 8-K records. That is the family PREREG-EVL-8's META-learners need to find forward where, if anywhere, intraday post-news drift lives. No designer ever sees an outcome, and the records are free, with no budget charge.

4. IT GIVES THE FIRST REAL MEASUREMENT OF CONTINUOUS-SESSION EXECUTION:
  - fill rate;
  - fills against the touch;
  - send lag;
  - markouts;
  - the non-fill selection (C4).
  This is the honest cost basis A96 asked for, for every later continuous lane and for the $30k plan's capacity. Its margins only ratchet toward stricter (C3).

5. IT FILLS DONE FAST ONCE IT PASSES. A promoted seat buys up to 14 Probe events a session from idle cash, at exactly its band size because of the B1 price cap. That is 50 Done events in about 4 sessions at full supply. Its exits use the touch replay, so Done's fill item is guarded by the EXEC HOLD.

6. IT FAILS CHEAPLY AND EARLY. EVL-6's RETIRE and the stricter-only LANE STOP (E4) end a losing lane at 200-400 shadow events. That frees budget for the next swing.
events_per_session_and_cost:
SUPPLY (calib/supply_idn.py).
- Inputs:
  - SPEED-FACTS' CTRL-NEWS-DAY-ON of 235/219/550 and EVL-NEWS-READ-ON of 54/54/142 (Oct 19/20/21);
  - HOUSE-FACTS' articles by UTC hour;
  - assumed filter shares, stated: FRESH 0.35-0.55, not KW_MOVE 0.80-0.90, ADV >= $20M 0.45-0.60, price <= 5% E 0.55-0.70, IEX quote ok 0.80-0.95, CONF price condition 0.15-0.32.
- The captain replaces the assumed shares with count_idn.py's outcome-free counts before the freeze. The rule does not depend on them.
- Estimates a session:
  - IDN candidates: 8.5-82.8.
  - EVL-IDN-READ-C: 2.1-21.4 (shadow K = 20).
  - EVL-IDN-CONF-C: 1.1-23.3.
  - Real money at learning: min(8, supply), i.e. 2.1-8 for READ and 1.1-8 for CONF. At Probe up to 14.
- Independence: one event per issuer per session; a 5-session cooldown; FRESH issuers have had no news or 8-K since the previous close.

LATENCY (calib/lat_idn.py, from code constants).
- Today: an article is stored p50 99 s after creation (at a 5 s Alpaca lag), and its first order is at the close auction.
- The lane: the order reaches the venue p50 65 s / p95 97 s after creation (90/122 s at a 30 s lag), and p50 42 s / p95 69 s after the House stores it.

COST PER EVENT (calib/cost_idn.py).
- Round trip = 2 x half-spread + 10 bp of margins + 0.32 bp of fees.
  - At half-spreads of 2/5/10/20/30 bp: 14.3/20.3/30.3/50.3/70.3 bp.
  - Gross drift needed to clear the screen's 10 bp margin: 24-80 bp.
  - For comparison, the auction replay charges an assumed 14-24 bp a round trip (EXECUTION-FACTS).
- Tuition at zero edge, learning size (8 lots of $37.96):
  - $0.62 a session at a 5 bp half-spread, $0.92 at 10 bp, $1.53 at 20 bp;
  - $12-31 over 20 sessions, against the $400 line;
  - a false Probe: $2.82 a session at 10 bp.
- Open risk at the 0.10 floor: $30 for 8 learning lots, $93 for 14 Probe lots.
- Capacity: 16% of E for one seat and 32% for two at learning, against about 45% of E idle.
- Orders: typically 2 a lot, at worst 4. The lane's line is 60.
- METERED COMPUTE: about $0 a day.
  - No new model call: the same PROMPT-NEWS and PROMPT-DOC rows, asked earlier.
  - SIP reads at night: about 1 + 2 x events + 2 + bars/25, i.e. roughly 150-250 a session, beside EVL-8's 1,640-1,790. Together that is under 10 minutes of the 200-a-minute plan.
  - The fast task makes at most about 12 requests a minute.

TIME TO DONE.
- There is no catch-up (B4). The first look is at the 22nd block after the release's first live session, i.e. late November at the earliest.
- At a true +60 bp after cost, P(promoted within 40 sessions) is 0.38-0.74 across 8-20 events a session and event scales 1.0/0.6 (calib/idn_frozen.py power).
- Once promoted, 50 Probe events take about 4 sessions at 14 a session, or about 25 at 2 a session.

risks: THE PRIOR IS WEAK. Busse & Green (2002) find positive TV stock reports priced within about a minute. Patell & Wolfson (1984) find wire news mostly priced within 5-10 minutes. Chordia, Green & Kottimukkalur (2018) find macro news priced within milliseconds. The House reaches the venue about 65-150 s after creation (lat_idn.py) and pays the spread. The most likely result is tuition of $0.6-1.5 a session a seat at learning, then RETIRE or the LANE STOP. This is a priced swing, not an expected profit.

SPEED: there is no catch-up (B4), so the seats' clock starts at the release, not at registration. The first possible promotion is the 22nd block, about late November. Even at a true +60 bp, P(promoted within 40 sessions) is only 0.38-0.74.

QUOTES: real time on the Basic plan is IEX only. IEX can be absent or wide for mid caps, which loses candidates under B1 (vii), and the NBBO is known only 16+ minutes later. The limit is set off IEX's ask, which is at or above the NBBO, so it errs toward filling. The fill then pays whatever the touch is, up to 30 bp above IEX.

ADVERSE SELECTION AND FILL RATE: spreads widen and depth falls around news (Gross-Klussmann & Hautsch 2011). A marketable buy after positive news fills mostly when the ask has not run. Non-fills drop out of both real money and the shadow under the same marketability rule; C4 measures the selection; the margins only ratchet stricter.

DONE'S FILL ITEM IS TWO-SIDED: price improvement beyond 15 bp fails it just as slippage does. The ADV >= $20M and 60 bp IEX spread caps bound the half-spread, and the EXEC HOLD stops entries at +-10 bp. Gaps from intraday fills mix with the auction rows' 0 bp gaps in Done's per-side mean.

CASH ACCOUNT: a buy funded by same-day unsettled proceeds and sold the same day is a good-faith violation. B6's settled-cash rule prevents it, but Alpaca's own reckoning is unread; data need 4 checks it. The existing O1 and ON pattern is unchanged by this lane.

SUPPLY IS UNCERTAIN: READ is estimated at 2.1-21.4 events a session and CONF at 1.1-23.3, from counts times assumed filter shares. At the low end the seats reach their minimums only by about session 15 and have little power.
BUDGET: LEFT is likely about 0.39 before READER-2 (G3), so probably only D1 seats. Raising the budget is the captain's call and costs 0.13 expected false passes a seat.
CORRELATED SEATS: D1 and D2 share stories, so their false passes are not independent. The budget charges both in full.

HOUSE LOAD: a new 30 s thread writes events.sqlite (WAL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, 30 s timeout) beside the record pass. Alpaca's 200-a-minute data limit is shared; the fast task uses about 12 requests a minute. A slow turn delays decided_at; that is recorded, never biased by price.

HALTS AND FAST MARKETS: a limit-up/limit-down pause after news leaves the quote stale, so the event is not TRADABLE. A resting order can still fill inside its 60 s once trading resumes. A halt at 15:40 pushes the lot to the closing-auction fallback, which then touches the close (counted).
KILL SWITCH: the gateway's kill switch also blocks sales, so intraday lots are held overnight under a kill, as every lot is.

VERDICT LINE: when the lane's $3 line is spent, READ candidates miss the 120 s condition. Events are lost but not biased. H-a's earlier asks change PREREG-EVL-5's 'answered by then' skips only in the frozen text's intended direction; this reading is recorded before the freeze.

IMPLEMENTATION: a fast-task bug could send many orders. The bounds are the gateway's STOCK_INTRADAY_MAX_DAY 40, its trading-hours and clock check, the House line of 60, the 10% name wall, the 1x book and the kill switch. Money code gets the adversarial money review.

SCOPE LIMITS: whole shares only, per the goal, so names above 5% of E are excluded. Fractional day orders would widen the universe, but only with the owner's say. Benzinga timestamp revisions are handled by the 10-minute live rule only.
